scope: Proposition 5.5 (The complete attached static base) of the manuscript “Equality and rigidity in the spacetime Penrose inequality” (preprints/Equality-and-rigidity-in-the-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4f1aab59ba484eb8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 48. statement: Let (Ω, g) be a smooth connected n- manifold, n ≥ 3, complete with its nonempty compact smooth boundary S = ⨆︁ℓ i=1 Si, 1 ≤ ℓ < ∞, included. Suppose the complement of a compact set is one Euclidean coordinate end. Let K, u, X be smooth up to the one-sided boundary, and suppose that, for some q0 > (n − 2)/2, g − δ = O2(r−q0 ), (u, X) = (b0 , b) + O2(r−q0 ), (b0 )2 − |b|2 = 1, b0 > 0. Assume u > 0 in the open exterior, u ≥ |X|g, and sym ∇X = −uK. On R × int Ω, set g = −u2 dz2 + gij(dxi + Xi dz)(dxj + Xj dz), ξ = ∂z, and assume Ricg(ξ, ·) = 0 throughout this interior spacetime and Ricg = 0 where W := u2 −|X|2 g > 0. On each connected boundary component Si, suppose X = uν, ∂νu + K(X, ν) = κi, κi > 0 constant, where ν points into Ω, and suppose either u > 0 throughout Si or u = 0 throughout it. Put α = X♭ g. On U = {W > 0} define λ = √ W, hs = g + W−1 α ⊗ α, C = h−1 s = g−1 − u−2 X ⊗ X, As = W−1 α, Fs = dAs. (5.14) Then U is connected and contains the end and a deleted collar of every Si. One has Fs = 0, and, writing h = hs, Hessh λ = λ Rich, ∆hλ = 0, Rh = 0, 0 < λ < 1. (5.15) The metric h has a smooth one-sided attachment at each Si, with induced metric g|TSi , zero second fundamental form, and ∂νh λ = κi. The attached base is complete with its boundary included. Every possible interior null frontier in the original exterior is infinitely far away for h. The even reflection of h and odd reflection of λ are C2,α for every 0 < α < 1, and the metric double is complete. After a fixed linear coordinate change, the given end of h is asymptotically Euclidean with O2(r−q0 ) decay.
